My family has worked this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know what grows here, and I know what the market wants. There's no mystery to it.

**My thinking:**

Quzhou is North China Plain — flat, decent soil, but dry. We depend on the groundwater well. Every farmer here does wheat in winter and corn in summer on the same land. That's how my father did it, that's how I do it. Ten mu total — all of it rotates between the two.

For wheat, I'll buy improved seeds from the county seed station again — probably Jimai 22 or whatever they're pushing this year. Better than the old stuff. I'll spread compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea at jointing. Four irrigations: one before sowing to get moisture up, one to help it through winter, one at jointing, one at grain filling. Two or three sprays — one for aphids in spring, maybe a fungicide if the weather's wet.

For corn, I go straight in after wheat harvest — no-till, just direct seeding. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar. Summer rains usually carry it through, but I'll pump twice if it's dry at silking. Corn needs a lot of nitrogen. I put down compound at planting and top-dress urea at the big bell stage.

I use rotary tillage on the wheat ground each autumn. Saves time, breaks up the surface well enough.
